text.p: Guyanor Resources SA said Monday a core drilling program started on the Chemin de Fer target on the St-Elie property in French Guiana, the third of several targets to be drilled on the property, which is owned jointly with Asarco Inc.

Guyanor, which is 68 percent owned by Golden Star Resources Ltd, said it and Asarco, through jointly owned Societe des Mines de St-Elie, have also negotiated with a local mining company, subject to government approval, an option on the Dieu-Merci property, which borders the St-Elie property to the east and south.

Guyanor said the Chemin de Fer target is situated in the southeast section of the 99-square kilometer St-Elie property. During late 1996, trenching was completed across the primary 1,400 by 200 meter Chemin de Fer anomaly.
The company said the average mineralized interval in the trenches was about 12 meters with a weighted average gold grade of 3.0 grames per metric tonne.
A second core drill is scheduled to be mobilized at St-Elie by the end of February for drilling on either the Chemin de Fer or Michel zones.

Following the construction of an additional exploration camp, access roads and drill pads, both drill rigs are scheduled to begin testing the new Dieu-Merci prospects in the near future, Guyanor said.

It said the Dieu-Merci property more than doubles the joint holdings in the region, to 254 square kilometers. Dieu-Merci hosts the southeastern extension of the Paramaca greenstone formation which trends through the St-Elie property and is also locally intruded by granites. The joint company negotiated a four-year option to earn an interest in the property. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
